plan: In a single-round auction with independent value draw, the optimal strategy is to bid strategically close to my true value. Since my private value is $31, I want to win without overpaying. I'll bid slightly above my value to increase winning chances, but not so high that I risk negative profit. A bid around $35-$37 seems reasonable - high enough to likely win, but not so high that I'll lose money if the second-highest bid is close to my true value.

In a single-round auction with independent value draws, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly below my true value. With my private value of $22, I want to win if possible, but avoid overpaying. Since values are uniformly distributed between $0-$49, other bidders might bid around their values too. I'll bid $20 - this leaves me a small profit margin if I win, and protects against overpaying if my value is higher than competitors.

My private value is $40. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is to bid my true value. If I bid less, I risk losing the item even when winning would be profitable. If I bid more, I might pay more than the item is worth to me. Since values are independent and randomly drawn, my best strategy is to bid $40 exactly, which maximizes my expected profit across potential opponent bid scenarios.
